Name: Liberal / Political Theory
Description: Philosophers primarily known for theories of individual rights, the social contract, constitutional government, and the proper limits and justification of state power.

Name: Analytic Philosophy
Description: The 20th-century tradition emphasizing logical rigor, careful conceptual analysis, and close engagement with language, science, and formal logic.

Name: Ancient Greek & Roman
Description: The classical schools of Greek and Roman antiquity, including Platonism, Aristotelianism, Stoicism, Epicureanism, and Skepticism.

Name: Existentialism / Phenomenology
Description: 20th-century movements centered on lived experience, consciousness, freedom, and the concrete situation of the individual human being.

Name: Confucian / Daoist / East Asian
Description: The classical and later Chinese schools -- Confucianism, Daoism, Mohism, and Legalism -- and their East Asian successors.

Name: Buddhist / Hindu / Jain
Description: The major philosophical schools of the Indian subcontinent built around liberation from suffering, including Buddhist, Hindu, and Jain traditions.

Name: Medieval / Scholastic Christian
Description: The Latin Christian philosophical tradition of the Middle Ages, synthesizing faith and reason through figures like Aquinas and Scotus.

Name: Marxism / Critical Theory
Description: Traditions analyzing society through material and economic structures, ideology, and power, from classical Marxism through the Frankfurt School.

Name: Post-structuralism / Postmodern Critique
Description: Late-20th-century movements questioning fixed structures of meaning, identity, and truth through genealogy, deconstruction, and discourse analysis.

Name: Empiricism
Description: The early modern and later tradition holding that knowledge derives primarily from sense experience rather than innate ideas or pure reason.

Name: German Idealism / Kantian
Description: The tradition following Kant that grounds reality and knowledge in the structuring activity of mind or spirit.

Name: Anti-colonial / Africana / Latin American
Description: 20th-century movements of political and cultural thought confronting colonialism, race, and identity in Africa, its diaspora, and Latin America.

Name: Islamic Philosophy
Description: The medieval Islamic philosophical tradition (falsafa), integrating Greek philosophy, Islamic theology, and mysticism.

Name: Rationalism (Early Modern)
Description: The 17th-century tradition holding that reason alone, rather than sense experience, is the primary source of certain knowledge.

Name: Feminism / Gender Theory
Description: Philosophical traditions analyzing gender, patriarchy, and the situation of women, from early feminist ethics to later gender theory.

Name: Pragmatism
Description: The American philosophical tradition holding that the meaning and truth of ideas are tied to their practical consequences.

Name: Renaissance Humanism
Description: The revival of classical learning, rhetoric, and civic virtue in Renaissance Europe.
